title: React
body:
A JavaScript library for building user interfaces out of **components** — self-contained functions that take inputs (props), hold their own state, and return a description of what should be rendered.

The central idea is that you stop imperatively mutating the [[DOM]] ("find this node, change its text") and instead declare what the UI should look like for a given state. When state changes, React re-renders the component, builds a new [[Virtual DOM]] tree, diffs it against the previous one, and applies only the minimal set of real DOM changes — see [[Reconciliation]]. That's why explicit `document.querySelector` calls largely disappear from React code.

It runs entirely on the user's machine, which makes a React app a textbook case of [[Client-Side Rendering]] (though frameworks built on it can also do [[Server-Side Rendering]]). It's the R in the MERN stack, alongside [[MongoDB]], [[Express]] and [[Node.js]].
